issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the problem UML declares a helper singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void, and the solution defines singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). In the template the parameter is commented out (signature: private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), so the template method has no Animal parameter. This mismatch between template and solution/problem statement will prevent students from calling singFarmSongVerse(animal) (e.g., from singFarmSong()) and will lead to compilation errors if they follow the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and solution. Change the template signature to: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... } (or protected if visibility is intentionally different per tests). Ensure the signature line in the template exactly matches the solution/problem specification.

issues.description: Visibility of Farm.singFarmSongVerse differs across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement indicates a private helper (minus sign) and the template declares the method as private, while the solution implements the method as protected. This discrepancy about access level may confuse students about the intended visibility and about whether subclasses or tests should be able to call the helper.
issues.suggestedFix: Make visibility consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution method to private to match the UML and template, or (B) update the UML/problem text and template to indicate protected if tests or intended design require subclass/test access. Ensure all three (problem statement, template, solution) use the same access modifier and update the template/solution accordingly.
